memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment: I would refuse any size on this coin.

The brief carries several hard disqualifiers. The class is FACTORY, which has lost about 46% on average. The curve shows bundle_share and top3_share at 1.0, meaning essentially all supply was bought through bundled, coordinated wallets, and the top-5 buyers hold 92% of first-2-minute buying. The launch bot was present, and sell-to-buy in the first two minutes was 0.047, so early liquidity was almost entirely one-directional.

The last-15-minute picture (+70% return, 495 buyers) looks like momentum, but it comes from a coin with concentrated early holders and a name ("SpaceX") that borrows a famous brand, which is a common pattern for trend-chasing rugs. Our 30-second fill lag would also put us in after a move we can't time.

No size, stop, or hold time makes this sane. If the desk wants exposure to coins like this, the only defensible setup is a pass. Skip.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak, and the brief doesn't support a real demand thesis.

The strongest-looking signals are momentum: a 171% return over 30 minutes, 495 buyers and about $30k volume in the last 15 minutes, and net inflow of 94 SOL. Price is still at its 30-minute high, so there's no drawdown yet.

But the curve data undercuts that. Bundle share is 1.0, top-3 share is 1.0, and the top-5 buyers account for 92% of early buying, which looks like coordinated accumulation rather than organic demand. The classification is FACTORY, the class with the worst base rate (about -46% per trade). The launch bot is present, and 66 buyers in the first two minutes against a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.047 suggests the early pool was nearly all one-directional. Sellers did show up later (339), so supply is already rotating, and the 30-minute high could be the top of a distribution rather than the start of a run.

Even the best-looking number, net flow, is dominated by a handful of wallets. Demand that will still be here in 30-60 minutes would show up as broad buyers and a falling bundle share, and neither is present.

Verdict: no honest case to buy. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a bundled insider distribution. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0, with 66 buyers in the first two minutes funded by a launch bot, and the top five buyers holding 92% of early volume. Its class is FACTORY, which has lost about 46% per trade on recent days, and the airdrop-dump check came back false only because it doesn't rule out a coordinated exit. The +172% run over 30 minutes (price 8.7e-6 SOL, $1.06M cap) sits on 77.5 SOL of sells against 171 SOL of buys in the last 15 minutes, with 339 sellers versus 495 buyers. The coin is already at its 30-minute high, so drawdown is zero and any reversal starts immediately. Against a 1.4-5.1% round trip, a modest dip from bundled holders wipes the expected move. The name "SpaceX" is a trademark-bait ticker that invites late retail chasing, which is exactly the exit liquidity the bundle needs. Skip.
